business_summary.text: Windsor Machines is a comprehensive solution provider in industrial manufacturing, specializing in CNC machines, injection moulding machinery, and extrusion machinery. The company has undergone significant strategic transformation with change of control in September 2024, acquisitions of Global CNC and Unitech Workholding, and consolidation of operations into a new integrated facility in Rajkot.

call_points.text: No specific financial guidance provided for FY27
EBITDA margins expected to recover as supply chain disruptions stabilize and pricing adjusts
Focus on operational discipline, deeper customer engagement, and building on integrated Rajkot facility
Management expects margin improvement as operational efficiencies stabilize post-transition
Export demand remains structurally intact, with stable revenues from Africa, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and MEA
SG&A expenses included one-time plant relocation cost of ₹4.8 Cr in FY26
₹725 Cr capital infusion through preferential issue completed, strengthening financial position

operating_notes.text: Manufacturing capacity increased to 3,600 machines p.a., expandable to 8,400 machines
One-time plant relocation cost of ₹4.8 Cr in FY26
Supply chain disruptions from Middle East conflict impacting raw material costs
Shift to agile 'Make-to-Stock' model for standard units, reducing delivery timelines from 2-3 months to 15-30 days
Export demand remains structurally intact, with stable export revenues to Africa, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and MEA region

timeline.summary: Windsor Machines completed strategic acquisitions of Global CNC and Unitech, shifted manufacturing to new Rajkot facility, and reported FY26 revenue growth of 54.7% YoY to ₹570.5 Cr

Windsor Machines reported Q1FY27 results with revenue growth of 31.4% YoY to ₹148.9 Cr, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.2% due to supply chain disruptions. Mohan Ramachandran joined as CEO, and the company continues to integrate operations at the new Rajkot facility.
